attributes.name: businessUnitName
attributes.rule: mirror: Business Units via: businessUnitID (display: businessUnitName)

Squads.description: Squads group People so that a manager can simulate forecastScopes by squad.

Regions.description: Geographical grouping of customers (ISO 9001:2015 §4.1 organisational context). A region can carry execution requirements of its own: Requirements may be scoped to specific regions (empty = applies to all regions).

attributes.name: countryName
attributes.notes: multivalued — countries this region covers (drives the Branches Country picker)

attributes.name: continent
attributes.notes: Derived — distinct continents of the selected countries (the Continent input was removed 2026-08-03; a region spanning several continents lists them all)

attributes.name: regionOwner
attributes.notes: Accountability owner (ISO 9001:2015 §5.3, §6.2.2(c)) — requirements-model.md asks rollup.userID; kept as the standard owner FK

Country.tooltip: Countries this region covers — offered as the Country options for the region's branches

Issues.description: Positive and negative factors or conditions for consideration (ISO 9001:2015 §4.1/§4.2). Positive issues are Opportunities — registered top-down by managers in strategic positions (SWOT or equivalent market analysis) to drive business strategy (segmentation, units, departments). Negative issues are Risks — elevated automatically from the nonconformity flow once an investigation routes a cause to the risk class (see issue #124).

attributes.name: issueName
attributes.notes: e.g., Lifetime Extension, Increase Capability, Dieletric Failure

attributes.name: businessUnitID
attributes.notes: Unit this issue classifies under (2026-08-03 reversal of the 2026-08-01 segment round — segment shows as the select group header)

attributes.name: scopeID
attributes.notes: Scopes tagged with this issue (reverse of Scopes.scopeOpportunity)

attributes.name: businessUnitTitle
attributes.notes: unitName-segmentName; hidden by default (the Unit column covers it)

Branches.description: Physical branches (internal factories/sites) of the organisation — segment, unit, region and country aware (stakeholder round 2026-08-01)

attributes.name: customerID
attributes.notes: Written from the CUSTOMER form (2026-08-03): registering a customer selects its branches and the save stamps customerID here — the Branches form has no Customer input. Nullable: a branch may have no customer yet.

attributes.name: countryName
attributes.notes: Country picker sourced from the hidden Countries registry

attributes.name: userID
attributes.notes: Branch owner — any person, options grouped by function

Country.tooltip: Only countries registered on the selected Region are offered
Country.field-rule: SelectLabel = continent; filtered by Region.countryName selected

Countries.description: System registry of countries per continent — predefined in data/countries.json, never user-registered; feeds the Branches Country picker

Customers.description: Manufacturing site entity (ISO §4.1 organisational context) with business segment classification: LPT (Large Power Transformers), MT (Medium Transformers), or DT (Distribution Transformers).

attributes.name: customerType
attributes.notes: Relationship of this customer to the organisation — branch (internal), client (external) or supplier

attributes.name: forecastID
attributes.notes: All forecast records belonging to this customer

attributes.name: scopeName
attributes.notes: All forecast records belonging to this customer

attributes.name: branchID
attributes.notes: Multivalued — branches registered to this customer. AUTHORED HERE: the Customer form's Branch picker writes customerID onto the selected Branch rows on save (applyCustomerBranches); nothing is stored on the Customer record.

periodFrame.default: last six months from current date

scopeName.field-rule: computed -> Scopes (via: forecasts), (display: scopeName):  Multivalued field

Type.tooltip: Relationship to the organisation: branch (internal), client (external) or supplier

Branch.tooltip: Branches this customer is registered at — saving writes the link onto the Branch records

Forecasts.description: A Forecast (ISO §6.1) groups a set of Forecast Scopes so that a Customer (factory) can project to global engineering its intended use of role resources for a given planning period.

attributes.name: businessUnitName
attributes.notes: Business Unit of the submitting customer — groups the Forecast select on the Forecast Scopes form

attributes.name: periodFinish
attributes.rule: computed: add periodType month quantity to startDate to find periodFinish
notes: if periodType = annual and periodStart = Mar/2026, than periodFinish = Mar/2027
if periodType = quarter and periodStart = Mar/2026, than periodFinish = Jun/2026
if periodType = month and periodStart = Mar/2026, than periodFinish = Mar/2026

attributes.name: periodBusinessDays
attributes.rule: computed: business days between periodStart and periodFinish. Apply USA business days calendar for this prototype
notes: if periodType = annual and periodStart = Mar/2026, than periodBusinessDays=254
if periodType = quarter and periodStart = Mar/2026, than periodBusinessDays=85
if periodType = month and periodStart = Mar/2026, than periodBusinessDays=22

attributes.name: weeklyUsageQuota
attributes.rule: computed: divide 'totalEstimatedHours' by the number of weeks in 'periodFrame'

attributes.name: forecastScopeID
attributes.notes: All child Forecast Scope records belonging to this forecast

attributes.name: scopeName
attributes.notes: All child Forecast Scope records belonging to this forecast

attributes.name: totalEstimatedHours
attributes.notes: Total demand projected across all scopes

Report-A.rule: Forecasts.forecastID.totalEstimatedHours vs Tickets.tickedID.ticketExecutionTime by customerName, Y = hours, X = customerName

periodFrame.default: last six months from current date

scopeName.field-rule: computed -> Scopes (via: eventTitle.field), (display: scopeName):  Multivalued field

Forecast Scopes.description: The atomic unit of a Forecast (ISO §6.1/§6.2). Specifies one Event × Product Scope combination; the Event determines the triggered Process and therefore the Tasks whose roles and execution times drive estimatedHours.

attributes.name: eventID
attributes.notes: Event that triggers the Process; determines the task list

attributes.name: requirementID
attributes.rule: computed → Requirements (via: forecastID.customerID.regionID + forecastID.customerID.businessUnitID + scopeID + productGroupID) (display: requirementName)
attributes.notes: Requirements linked to the row's scope + product group

attributes.name: productScopeID
attributes.rule: computed → Product Scopes (via: eventID + productGroupID + scopeID + requirementName)

attributes.name: processID
attributes.notes: Process triggered by the selected Event

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.notes: Tasks matching this event and product scope

attributes.name: functionName
attributes.notes: Roles derived from Tasks in the triggered Process

attributes.name: estimatedHours
attributes.notes: Total execution hours across all Tasks

attributes.name: region
attributes.notes: Region of the factory that owns the parent forecast (via forecastID → Customers.regionID → Regions). Used by Report-B.

attributes.name: forecastScopeQuantity
attributes.notes: amount of forecast scope to be used to calculate estimatedHours

attributes.name: consumption
attributes.rule: computed: every time an forecastScopeID is added to a Ticket this column should be added by 1

Report-A.rule: forecastScopeID.estimatedHours grouped by productScopeID (scope name), stacked by roles

periodFrame.default: last six months from current date

Forecast.field-rule: SelectLabel = businessUnitName; WHERE periodFinish >= current month

Tasks.description: A Task is the application of an action to a process activity (workflow). It serves only as an execution template; concrete Jobs are created from Tasks in the Workspace module (where taskOwner, taskStatus, taskDueDate and projectID are set).

attributes.name: processID
attributes.notes: Stored FK (materialize-FK convention) — the process of the selected event; the form filters the options by the Event field. The old "rollup: from eventID" prose made the parser resolve the TARGET as the Events table (fuzzy id-suffix match), so the Process select offered eventIDs (2026-08-04 bug).

attributes.name: actionID
attributes.rule: computed: lookup Actions via activityID (display: actionName)

attributes.name: requirementName
attributes.notes: Derived — requirements of the task's procedures (doctrine: tasks are requirement-free, the procedure carries the requirement set; empty set = applies to all, Q1)

attributes.name: functionID
attributes.notes: multivalued — derived from the competences referencing this task

attributes.name: executionTime
attributes.notes: Derived — procedures create the variance in task duration (Rafael, 04/08): the requirement set changes how long a task takes, so the time is registered PER PROCEDURE and the task shows the sum of its procedures.

attributes.name: competenceID
attributes.rule: rollup -> Competence via: taskID -> functionID (display: competenceName)

attributes.name: procedureID
attributes.notes: Procedures registered for this task (subitem tab)

Report-A.rule: Count of Tasks grouped by processID

Report-B.rule: Count of Tasks grouped by functionName

Process.field-rule: The process options will be filtered by the event selected

Activity.field-rule: The Activity options will be filtered by the process selected

Card 1-1.title: Recurrent tasks acrros Processes

card-rules.main-data: Top 3 tasks that appears in multiple processes
card-rules.detail-data: this card must be a list with two columns: taskID | process count

Card 1-1.card-tooltip: Most recurring tasks across the process landscape, indicating key operational dependencies.

Events.description: An Event is an aggregator of processes; it is not executed itself but triggers a defined execution. Forecasts group which events and execution parameters (forecastScopes) they contain. Corrective-action and nonconformity linkage is deferred to a future module.

attributes.name: departmentID
attributes.notes: Department handling the event — offered from the selected Business Unit's departments

attributes.name: tasks
attributes.notes: Tasks existing for each process triggered by this event

attributes.name: executionTime
attributes.notes: Sum over the event's tasks — each task in turn sums its procedures (nested derived sum)

attributes.name: forecastScopes
attributes.notes: Forecast Scopes that use this event to estimate workload

Department.tooltip: Departments of the selected Business Unit

Processes.description: The Process table groups workflows. The user creates a process item that is later used to build the process steps (workflow) records.

attributes.name: processSystemID
attributes.notes: Optional external registry system ID reference; not mandatory

attributes.name: squadID
attributes.notes: Squad running the process — offered from the squads of the department reached through the selected Event (eventID → departmentID)

attributes.name: targetExecutionTime
attributes.notes: Average execution time across task groups sharing the same action + workflow combination

attributes.name: activities
attributes.notes: Activities of this process, reached through its workflow steps

attributes.name: tasks
attributes.notes: All Tasks belonging to this Process

attributes.name: productName
attributes.notes: From tasks rollup, for report filtering

attributes.name: businessUnitID
attributes.notes: Distinct unit(s) of the process events, for report filtering

attributes.name: scopeName
attributes.notes: From tasks rollup, for report filtering

Report-A.rule: Count of Tasks grouped by processName

Description.tooltip: Give a description for the process

Event.tooltip: The event that triggers the process

Squad.tooltip: Squads of the department handling the selected Event

Activities.description: Hidden registry (dashboard-order 0) of the activities that form workflow steps (step = activity x process, v3-review D3). Created inline via the '+' button on the Workflows Activity select -- FK-keyed, no free text, so grouping/filtering never breaks on typos.

attributes.name: actionID
attributes.notes: All actions derived from this Activity

Description.tooltip: Give a description for the Activity

Workflows.description: Registry of the steps of each process. Through the relations of its records users understand how a process should be executed in terms of activities.

attributes.name: activityID
attributes.notes: The activity this step executes (step = activity × process); stored FK since v3-review R5 — was a dead rollup

attributes.name: parentStepID
attributes.notes: Self-referential step ordering (nullable — first step of a process has no parent). Displays the step's ACTIVITY name (Rafael, 04/08), resolved through the step's activityID.

attributes.name: indentationID
attributes.notes: Derived outline number (1, 2, 2.1, 3…) — never stored; computed per process from the parent-step chain. Sequential rules (start-to-finish, finish-to-start) take the next major number, parallel rules (finish-to-finish, start-to-start) sub-number under the parent. See identation-rule.md.

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.notes: Tasks that use this workflow item

Parent Step.tooltip: Previous step of the SAME process that feeds this one — options are the steps already registered for the selected process. Leave empty for the first step (it takes the next major number; steps with a parent sub-number under it).
Parent Step.field-rule: filtered by Process selected; display workflowID.activityName

Indentation Rule.tooltip: Dependency on the parent step: sequential rules (start-to-finish, finish-to-start) place this step after the parent; parallel rules (finish-to-finish, start-to-start) nest it under the parent. The step number (indentationID) is derived automatically.

Actions.description: An action defines the procedure to be performed to execute a given step (workflow) within a process.

attributes.name: activityID
attributes.notes: From taskID rollup; allows filtering by activity

attributes.name: workflowID
attributes.notes: From taskID rollup; allows filtering by workflow (activity + process)

Handouts.description: Input or output document/deliverable exchanged between process steps (ISO §4.4.2(b) — retained documented information).

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.notes: All tasks that use this handout as input or output

attributes.name: processID
attributes.notes: Chain inherited from the task(s) referencing this handout

attributes.name: workflowID
attributes.notes: Chain inherited from the task(s) referencing this handout

attributes.name: actionID
attributes.notes: Chain inherited from the task(s) referencing this handout

Channel.tooltip: Tool, app or system used to store or manage the handout

Channels.description: Communication or delivery channel used in process steps, with assigned owner (ISO §7.4).

attributes.name: channelOwner
attributes.notes: Company or person responsible for managing the channel

attributes.name: handouts
attributes.notes: All Handouts delivered through this channel

Procedures.description: Documented method for executing a Task (ISO 9001:2015 §4.4 operations chain; §7.5 documented information). Tasks stay requirement-free — the procedure is where requirements bite: each row registers how a task is performed under a given requirement set, with its own input/output handouts. An empty requirement list means the procedure applies to every requirement (Q1 wildcard).

attributes.name: procedureRegistry
attributes.notes: External registry number / unique identification (label attribute)

attributes.name: businessUnitID
attributes.notes: Form filter — narrows the Department options

attributes.name: departmentID
attributes.notes: Form filter — narrows the Process options

attributes.name: processID
attributes.notes: Form filter — narrows the Task options

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.notes: Task this procedure executes — join anchor for the Tasks → Procedures subitem tab

attributes.name: requirementID
attributes.notes: Multivalued; nullable — requirements under which this procedure applies. EMPTY = applies to all (Q1 wildcard). Form options are filtered to the selected task's derived requirement set (via its workflow, 5-key chain).

attributes.name: taskInput
attributes.notes: Multivalued — input handouts of this procedure (moved from Tasks — iterations round A5); form options follow the owning chain (unlinked handouts always offered)

attributes.name: taskOutput
attributes.notes: Multivalued — output handouts of this procedure (moved from Tasks — iterations round A5); form options follow the owning chain (unlinked handouts always offered)

attributes.name: executionTime
attributes.notes: Hours to execute the task under THIS procedure's requirement set — moved from Tasks (2026-08-04): procedures create the variance in task duration

Registry Code.tooltip: Registry number or unique identification for the procedure

Process.field-rule: SelectLabel = squadName; filtered by Department selected

Requirements.tooltip: Requirements under which this procedure applies — leave empty when it applies to all

Procedure URL.tooltip: Link to access the procedure documentation

Inputs.field-rule: Allow multiple values; filtered by Process + Activity + Action selected

Outputs.field-rule: Allow multiple values; filtered by Process + Activity + Action selected

Execution Time.tooltip: Hours to execute the task under this procedure's requirement set

Product Scopes.description: Combination of product and scope used for planning and forecasting execution demand (ISO §4.3 / §8.1).

attributes.name: productScopeID
attributes.notes: Displayed as a group code, e.g. "AA"

attributes.name: businessUnitID
attributes.notes: Derived on save from the selected Product Group (no user input)

attributes.name: productGroupID
attributes.notes: Options show productName | SPECS and are filtered by the selected Business Unit (via the group's products)

attributes.name: productSpecName

attributes.name: requirementID
attributes.rule: rollup → Requirements (via: productGroupID + scopeID + businessUnitID) (display: requirementName)
attributes.notes: Requirements linked to this scope + product group pair

Scopes.description: Defines the work scope boundaries applicable to products (e.g., Uprating, Temperature Reduction, Redesign) — ISO §4.3.

attributes.name: productScopeID
attributes.rule: computed: list productScopeID from Product Scopes where scopeID matches

Opportunity.field-rule: SelectLabel = issueType; filtered by Business Unit.businessSegmentID selected

Products.description: Power transformer products and services tracked through quality and forecasting cycles (ISO §8.1).

Owner.field-rule: SelectLabel = functionName; filtered by businessUnitID selected

Product Specs.description: Dynamic attribute definitions for Product Groups: each spec becomes an input field in the Product Group form for the products it applies to (ISO §8.1).

Product Groups.description: Higher-level commercial grouping of product classes for planning (ISO §8.1).

Specs.tooltip: Spec attributes of the selected Product

attributes.name: businessUnitID

attributes.notes: multivalued — scopes this requirement applies to

Product Group.field-rule: Allow multiple values; filtered by businessUnitID selected

Projects.description: Engineering project with customer/factory, owner and status. Groups tickets and provides estimated vs. executed time roll-ups (ISO §8.3 / §8.4).

Jobs.description: A Job is a concrete execution record assigning a person/role to a Ticket to perform a piece of work, tracking planned and actual dates, dependencies and status. Jobs are the primary source of actual usage data for the Control module (ISO §7.1.2).

attributes.name: projectID
attributes.notes: Project the job belongs to (via its ticket)

attributes.name: scopeID
attributes.rule: rollup → Product Scopes via: ticketID (display: scopeName)
attributes.notes: Scope of the ticket's product scope

attributes.name: productGroupID
attributes.rule: rollup → Product Scopes via: ticketID (display: productGroupName)
attributes.notes: Product group of the ticket's product scope

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.rule: rollup → Tasks (via: customerID + productGroupID + scopeID) (display: taskName)
attributes.notes: Task template; options filtered by the ticket's customer + product group + scope

attributes.name: userID
attributes.notes: Filtered by the roleID of the selected task template

attributes.rule: computed: use taskID.estimatedTime to calculate the start date

attributes.name: plannedExecutionTime

attributes.name: realExecutionTime

attributes.name: stoppedAt

attributes.name: squadName

Capacity.description: Query view (Control module) — no new-item form. Aggregates role/department capacity against allocation over a planning period (ISO §7.1.2 / §6.2).

attributes.name: functionName
attributes.notes: Function of the role (via roleID → Roles.functionID). Used by Report-A/B filters.

attributes.name: availableHours
attributes.notes: computed: sum of People.workingHours (weekly) for the function, scaled to the number of weeks in the selected period (Σ periodBusinessDays/5). Factory-independent — used by Report-A as available capacity per function.

attributes.name: allocatedHours
attributes.rule: computed: sum of Forecast Scopes.estimatedHours grouped by functionName, for forecasts within the selected customer + period
attributes.notes: totalEstimatedHours decomposed by function (= its Forecast Scopes). Used by Report-A as allocated demand per function; responds to the factory + period filters and the Exclude-Draft radio.

Report-A.rule: availableHours vs. allocatedHours side by side grouped by functionName. Y = hours, X = functionName. Apply the weeklyUsageQuota for allocatedHours time framing for the period selected in the filter

periodFrame.default: last six months from current date

scopeName.field-rule: computed -> Scopes (via: eventTitle.field), (display: scopeName):  Multivalued field

Branch.tooltip: Branch this person is stationed at — optional

Onboarding.description: Tracks a person's certification progress against the competences derived from their function and roles (ISO §7.2).

attributes.name: departmentID
attributes.notes: Department running the onboarding; businessUnitID derives from it on save

attributes.name: roleID
attributes.notes: Role resolved from the onboarding's function (Roles.functionID); display: roleName via the Roles table which owns that field.

attributes.name: competenceID
attributes.notes: Stores the competence PK; role/rank/department narrowing lives in the form cascade (the old 'via: roleID + levelRank' spelling made the select store roleIDs)

attributes.name: requirementName
attributes.rule: computed: Competence via competenceID (display: FOREACH([{requirementTypeName: requirementName}]))

Talent.field-rule: SelectLabel = functionName; filtered by departmentID selected

Competence.tooltip: Competences of the selected Department (via their event) matching the chosen Role
Competence.field-rule: SelectLabel = processName; filtered by departmentID + roleID selected

Competence.description: Competence profile mapping skills to roles, scopes and products (ISO §7.2), derived largely from the Tasks a role performs.

attributes.name: departmentID
attributes.notes: Derived on save from the selected Event (Event.departmentID) — join key for the Onboarding Department → Competence cascade

attributes.name: processID
attributes.notes: Process context for the certified task

attributes.name: scopeID
attributes.notes: Scope this competence certifies (links Product Scopes → Competence subitems)

attributes.name: roleID
attributes.notes: Filtered by the selected function + skill level in the form

attributes.name: levelRank
attributes.notes: Step of the professional INSIDE the competence's skill level (Rafael, 03/08): rank 1 = a newly promoted/hired professional at that level may hold the competence; holding rank 3 on every competence of a skill level signals readiness to move up a level (promotion automation: issue #149)

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.notes: Task this competence certifies; options filtered by event + process

attributes.name: productSpecID
attributes.notes: multivalued — spec definitions certified by this competence

attributes.name: productSpecName
attributes.rule: computed: Product Specs via productSpecID (display: specName)

attributes.name: procedureID
attributes.notes: Multivalued — procedures this competence certifies (a procedure can be held by many competences)

attributes.name: requirementID
attributes.notes: Derived — requirements certified through the linked procedures (a procedure with an empty set applies to all, Q1)

attributes.name: competenceName
attributes.rule: computed: CONCAT([taskName],' for ',[scopeName],' of ',[productGroupName],' applied to ',[{requirementTypeName: requirementName}])
attributes.notes: Rendered from the CONCAT rule at display time (not stored)

attributes.name: channelName
attributes.rule: computed: list of channelName of every input and output handout of the linked procedures

Role.field-rule: filtered by Skill Level + Function selected

Procedure.tooltip: Procedures of the selected task that this competence certifies
